ogTitle: 10 Most Popular Restaurants in Uthai Thani 2026 — Eat Like a Local
ogDesc: From Kotung Khao Man Kai and Jae Nok braised chicken noodles of Trok Rong Ya, Phaiphan sangkaya-filled bread, fresh Sakae Krang river fish, to Ya Jaew Coconut Ice Cream — 10 great spots in Uthai Thani you should try.
intro: Uthai Thani is a small city on the Sakae Krang River where you can eat well at any hour of the day. The charm is in the decades-old restaurants along Trok Rong Ya and the old-town area — from khao man kai and braised chicken noodles to fresh river fish and beloved desserts. We've gathered the 10 restaurants that locals and travellers mention most, covering every meal from breakfast through the evening sweet.
chips: 🍗 Kotung Khao Man Kai — open for nearly 60 years
🍜 Jae Nok braised chicken noodles, Trok Rong Ya — sold out before noon
🐟 Fresh Sakae Krang river fish by the water
☕ Som za coffee — a local Uthai Thani citrus
🍦 Ya Jaew Coconut Ice Cream — just a few baht a cup

blocks.html:
To talk about eating in Uthai Thani, you have to start in the old town and Trok Rong Ya — a small walking street lined with old wooden shophouses, vintage coffee shops, and restaurants that have been open since the owner's parents were young. Early morning brings Hainanese khao man kai and hand-brewed coffee for a few dozen baht a cup. Late morning you walk over for braised chicken noodles in a rich, deep broth, followed by sangkaya-filled bread — so loaded it oozes — to take as a souvenir. When the afternoon turns cooler you head down to the Sakae Krang River, order whole fried pla rad with garlic, and sit with the breeze. That's the Uthai Thani rhythm — slow, easy, and genuinely good.

Every restaurant on this list has its own story. Kotung Khao Man Kai Uthai Thani has been open since 1967 — nearly sixty years — starting as a small cart run by Uncle Kotung before becoming a legendary Shell Recommends institution. Jae Nok Chicken Noodles Trok Rong Ya is an ancient recipe that sells out before noon almost every day. Phaiphan Sangkaya Bread is the shop that made sangkaya-filled bread the signature souvenir of the province. Jae Da Fish Blanched is a legendary blanche-and-dip restaurant that has stood near the clock tower for generations. And if you want something new, TONE CAFE has taken som za — a local Uthai citrus — and created a som za coffee signature that everyone makes a point of trying. Read through and plan your Uthai Thani eating trip.

blocks.name: Kotung Khao Man Kai Uthai Thani
blocks.area: Tha Chang Road, Uthai Mai Subdistrict, Mueang Uthai Thani District, Uthai Thani
blocks.signature: Free-range Hainanese khao man kai, house fermented-soybean dipping sauce, pork satay
blocks.descHtml:
If you arrive in Uthai Thani for the first time and don't know where to start for your first meal, Kotung Khao Man Kai is the restaurant almost every local will point you to. The old shophouse on Tha Chang Road, opposite the Thai Military Bank, has been open since 1967 — starting as a cart run by Uncle Kotung (Prasit Yangyuensin) — and is now a legendary Shell Recommends institution that has been part of the city for almost sixty years. A great fit for anyone who wants traditional Hainanese-style khao man kai in a setting that's honest and unpretentious.

The star is the free-range khao man kai — plump chicken, poached until the meat is firm and tender, skin a clean golden colour. Most reviews praise the tender chicken, the rice cooked in fragrant broth that's perfectly rich without being heavy, and the dipping sauce that comes in two versions: the house fermented soybean sauce with chopped ginger and sliced chilli, and a bold seafood dipping sauce. Either version takes the dish in a different direction, and the dipping sauce is what most people say keeps them coming back. Another dish many order alongside is the pork satay — grilled fragrant, excellent with the peanut dipping sauce.

Beyond the khao man kai, there's also goat braised with Chinese herbs, bamboo shoot soup, fish maw soup, red pork and crispy pork rice, duck rice on rice, and house-made hoi jor — all good for ordering to share in a group. Prices start in the low tens per dish, averaging around 60–80 THB per person — strong value for an institution of this reputation.

The restaurant opens from around 06:00 through 14:30 daily. Those planning to come for breakfast or lunch should arrive before items sell out. Parking is available and the sign is clear. Some reviews note the drink counter looks a little worn in keeping with the original-style décor, but for flavour and the feel of a genuine Uthai institution, there's a reason people never stop coming.
mustOrder: Red pork and crispy pork rice
blocks.bestFor: First breakfast or lunch in Uthai Thani

blocks.name: Jae Nok Chicken Noodles Trok Rong Ya
blocks.area: Trok Rong Ya, Uthai Mai Subdistrict, Mueang Uthai Thani District
blocks.signature: Ancient-recipe braised chicken noodles, rich broth, fall-apart tender chicken
blocks.descHtml:
If you're wandering Trok Rong Ya in the old town of Uthai Thani and your stomach starts talking, the first restaurant locals will point you to is Jae Nok — a wooden shophouse that has been serving noodles across generations for over 70 years. Jae Nok herself has been at the pot for over 40 of those years. The star is the ancient-recipe braised chicken noodles — chicken simmered until fall-apart tender, in an aromatic broth balanced with fragrant oil and dry-roasted chilli for a rounded flavour that's genuinely hard to find in big cities. A great fit for anyone who wants a slow, easy traditional meal in a laid-back atmosphere.

The dish almost every table orders is the braised chicken noodles — generous toppings, big torn chicken pieces, meat tender to the core and full of flavour. Another regular order from loyal customers is the bounce-pork (moo deng) noodles — chewy, pleasurable eating. Multiple genuine reviews agree: the broth is fragrant, with a gentle hint of roasted chilli and just a touch of sweetness; the braised chicken dissolves on the tongue. Many reviewers also mention that Jae Nok herself is warm and friendly, which makes the whole meal better.

Prices are very light — regular noodles start around 40 THB; a full bowl of braised chicken or moo deng around 50 THB. Under 100 THB per person and you'll be satisfied. Open daily 09:30–15:00. Located at 50 Ratsadutit Road, Uthai Mai Subdistrict — easy to walk to from anywhere in the old-town area.

One thing to know: the restaurant sells out fast and some items can be gone by around 11:30 on busy days. If you want the full braised-chicken bowl with all the toppings, aim for late morning to noon. This is a restaurant that makes both Uthai locals and visitors willing to queue — because you simply can't get a genuinely old-style braised chicken noodle at this price anywhere else.
blocks.bestFor: Mid-morning to noon in the old town — genuine ancient braised chicken noodles

blocks.name: Phaiphan Sangkaya Bread
blocks.area: Mueang Uthai Thani District, Uthai Thani
blocks.signature: Bread fully injected with sangkaya custard filling, buttery and soft
blocks.descHtml:
If you ask Uthai Thani locals which souvenir shop is unmissable, Phaiphan always comes up first. This is the original sangkaya-filled bread shop of the province — open for nearly 50 years, since the original Phaiphan received a pound-bread recipe from an Australian missionary and figured out how to inject sangkaya custard fully inside each roll, making it the most distinctive souvenir of the city. Today the next generation runs it, making and selling only from this single location — no branches, no franchise. A great fit for anyone who wants a genuinely authentic local souvenir to take home, or dessert-lovers wanting to try the original city speciality.

The dish to order is the bread fully injected with sangkaya custard. The charm here is a soft, buttery roll — bite in and the orange sangkaya filling oozes out in what many people call "lava sangkaya" because it's more liquid than anywhere else. The sweetness is well-calibrated, not sharp, with a rounded egg-and-coconut note that contrasts with the dough perfectly. Most reviews praise the fact that the filling isn't cloying — each piece is enjoyable without getting heavy. Some people prefer buying it still warm, which delivers the fullest butter flavour and the softest filling.

Sold by the box: one box contains 10 pieces, priced well under a hundred baht — strong value for something baked fresh. The shop bakes in batches by order, so items often sell out, especially on long holidays and festivals. Those specifically making the trip should call ahead to reserve, or arrive before noon — afternoons and evenings regularly see a sold-out sign.

Located in the city centre on Si Uthai Road in the Tha Chang area, Uthai Mai Subdistrict, opposite the Krung Thai Bank — easy to spot, easy to park and stop. Open from 07:30 to around 16:00–16:30 daily. This shop is famous precisely because it's the original, only place making sangkaya in this style for this long — and it's become part of the city. Anyone passing through Uthai Thani without stopping in has genuinely missed one of the province's best things.
mustOrder: Bread fully injected with sangkaya custard
Plain pound loaf with sangkaya for dipping
blocks.bestFor: Authentic city souvenir to take home / dessert lovers

blocks.name: Jae Da Fish Blanched
blocks.area: Mueang Uthai Thani District, Uthai Thani
blocks.signature: Blanched pla rad with standout seafood dipping sauce, crispy pork fried in fish sauce, dry tom yam mixed platter
blocks.descHtml:
If you ask Uthai Thani locals where to eat dinner, Jae Da Fish Blanched is consistently one of the first names that comes up. This rice porridge and sides restaurant on Tha Chang Road, near the clock tower roundabout and the Witthayu five-way junction, has been a three-generation family operation. The main draw is fresh river fish from the Sakae Krang, with the signature dish — blanched pla rad with dipping — standing at the centre of every table. The fish is firm and naturally sweet, served with three dipping sauces: bold seafood sauce, sweet-sour fermented soybean, and sweet sauce, to alternate as you like. A great fit for those who want river fish with none of the muddy smell.

Beyond the blanched fish, dishes mentioned frequently are the crispy pork fried in fish sauce — many reviews describe it as properly crunchy and enjoyable — and the dry tom yam mixed platter, with a bold, rounded hot-sour flavour. Those who like simpler dishes can also order garlic-fried soft-flesh fish, Chinese kale with salted fish, stir-fried water spinach, pickled sausage salad, and fresh prawns in fish sauce. Most individual dishes run around 80–100 THB; averaging 101–250 THB per person — fair value for fresh river fish of this quality.

The atmosphere is a casual rice porridge style — tables set along the roadside, not a big restaurant, but consistently packed every evening. Both locals and travellers keep coming. Review scores sit around 4.0 from hundreds of reviewers, confirmed by a User Choice award and appearing in nearly every "what to eat in Uthai" list.

The restaurant only opens evenings: daily 16:30–21:00. Peak times can mean a wait, though most food arrives within around 20 minutes. Seating is roadside and open-air — evenings can bring mosquitoes and warmth, so a small repellent is worth carrying. Roadside parking is available beside the restaurant. A great evening meal format for groups ordering multiple sharing plates.
mustOrder: Blanched pla rad with seafood dipping sauce
Crispy pork fried in fish sauce
blocks.bestFor: Evening group dinner with river fish
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: tom yam · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Pa Thong Traditional Coffee
blocks.area: Tha Chang Road, Mueang Uthai Thani District, Uthai Thani
blocks.signature: Hand-brewed old-school coffee at 10 THB a cup, free pa thong ko (fried dough), soft-boiled egg
blocks.descHtml:
If you wake up in Uthai Thani and want to start the day the way the locals do, Pa Thong's old-school coffee shop is the stop to make. A small shop in an old wooden building on Tha Chang Road, near the elephant roundabout, opposite Dr Wirat's herbal medicine shop — Pa Thong has been hand-brewing coffee right here for over fifty years. The walls are covered with photos of famous visitors; there's a vintage TV, old coffee and tea cups, an atmosphere of an all-day community café where old and young sit and talk. A great fit for those who want a traditional breakfast at easy prices and want to absorb the old-town Uthai charm more than a prettily decorated café can offer.

The dish to order is the hand-brewed old-school coffee at 10 THB a cup. Pa Thong has always used Goat Brand coffee, brewed strong in the classic way — low sweetness, rounded, smooth. Available hot or as oliang (iced black). Pair it with two gently warm soft-boiled eggs at 15 THB, and note that pa thong ko (Chinese fried dough) and tea come free to dip in the coffee old community-café style. Most reviews agree the coffee is fragrant and genuinely strong, the soft-boiled eggs are done right, and — something everyone mentions without fail — Pa Thong herself is warm and kind, greeting every customer like an old acquaintance.

What makes this place talked about isn't just the coffee — it's the fact that Pa Thong has been brewing coffee here long enough to become part of the city's morning rhythm. Everything is in the double-digit price range; a complete breakfast costs well under a hundred baht. That's why it's popular with both locals and visitors wanting something real.

One thing to know: the shop opens very early — around 05:00 — and closes in the afternoon. For the lively community-café atmosphere, come in the morning. It's a small wooden shophouse with limited seating and no real parking — walking from the elephant roundabout area is easier. When you arrive, say hello to Pa Thong — it's a charm no other cup of coffee can replace.
blocks.bestFor: Local-style breakfast before exploring the old town
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: café · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.title: 🛏️ Stay in the Uthai Thani old town — walk to eat all day
blocks.text: The best restaurants in Uthai Thani are clustered in the old town and Trok Rong Ya. If you stay in the city or near the Sakae Krang River, you can walk to a morning meal, stop at a café, then stroll down to eat river fish in the evening without having to drive and hunt for parking. Pick a well-located stay first and spend the rest of your time eating.

blocks.name: Jae Nei Egg Noodles Uthai Thani
blocks.area: Mueang Uthai Thani District, Uthai Thani
blocks.signature: House-made thin egg noodles, tossed in sweet-spicy sauce, with red pork, fish balls
blocks.descHtml:
If you had to pick one bowl of noodles that represents Uthai Thani, most locals would name Jae Nei — a long-established restaurant open for over 80 years, near the Witthayu five-way junction, opposite the city pillar shrine, on Tha Chang Road walking a little further toward the Sakae Krang River. The star here is house-made egg noodles made fresh daily — a deep yellow colour, thin but springy and tender. Many people say the look and texture resemble instant-noodle thinness but the egg fragrance is far greater. This restaurant is best for those searching for genuine local flavours you can't find elsewhere, and for those who prefer dry tossed noodles over soup.

The menu here is straightforward in the style of a legendary restaurant: dry noodles or soup, with or without chilli, around 45 THB; fish maw around 50 THB. Toppings are red pork, minced pork, and fish balls. The star is the dry noodles tossed in sauce mixed in the kitchen to the right level — flavour leads with sweetness then a gentle chilli kick. Eats clean almost without needing any seasoning added. Many reviews praise the distinctively soft noodles and the tender red pork. Those who like springy noodles in a rounded sauce will find this addictive.

The restaurant has been renovated and looks cleaner and more comfortable than before. Open mid-morning to early afternoon, roughly 09:30–15:00, and often sells out early on busy days. Note that Jae makes everything herself as the main cook, so peak times may mean a short wait — patience is rewarded. Some reviewers mention the tom yam broth's sourness doesn't suit them as well as the dry version; if this is your first visit, the dry noodles with chilli are the recommended opening order — you'll understand quickly why Uthai locals consider this the city's noodle.
blocks.bestFor: Mid-morning tasting of the city's legendary noodles

blocks.name: TONE CAFE
blocks.area: Trok Rong Ya, old town, Mueang Uthai Thani District
blocks.signature: Som Za Coffee (local citrus coffee signature) and special coffee drinks
blocks.descHtml:
Anyone walking through the Trok Rong Ya old-town walking street in Uthai Thani and looking for a quiet spot to sit and sip coffee will find TONE CAFE right there — a small café tucked into a lane off the walking street, just a short walk from the old market. The building is a warm wooden shophouse with photo spots both inside and out, a small number of tables and comfortable seating, better suited for a quiet sit than a large group outing.

The star here is the Som Za Coffee — taking som za, a local Uthai citrus, and pairing it with coffee. Everyone who has tried it agrees: a pleasant sour-sparkle that cuts through the coffee in just the right balance, freshly fragrant like a citrus soda but with more depth. Beyond this signature, there's also Orange Tonic, Apple Cider Coffee, coconut coffee, Mojito Espresso, and Matcha Latte. For those who prefer strong flavours, multiple reviewers say the drinks are well-made and rival good café output you'd find in Bangkok. There's also boobun bread from the neighbouring shop — coconut cream filling eaten warm, a perfect pairing.

Drink prices start around 68 THB; specialty drinks like the som za coffee run around 80–129 THB — fair value for the quality. Open daily 08:30–16:30. One thing to know: there's no parking in front of the café — park near the old market or on the walking street and walk in. Sometimes the door is closed to keep the air conditioning in even when the café is open — just push it and step inside.

TONE CAFE is popular among Uthai visitors because it makes something fun and genuinely good with a local ingredient. The flavour is fresh and real; the old-town atmosphere helps. It's a well-timed stop for café-lovers wanting something that can only be found here.
mustOrder: Boobun bread with coconut cream filling
blocks.bestFor: Café-lovers wanting a local-citrus coffee mid-morning or afternoon while exploring the old town

blocks.name: Ruean Phae Pramong
blocks.signature: Garlic-fried pla rad and fresh Sakae Krang river fish
blocks.descHtml:
If you come to Uthai Thani and want fresh river fish in an atmosphere that simply doesn't exist in big cities, Ruean Phae Pramong is the name Uthai locals mention first. The restaurant is on a wooden raft floating on the Sakae Krang River — open for over thirty years, making it the pioneering raft house of this stretch. The experience involves walking down a wooden gangway from the riverbank to sit on a raft actually out on the water. A great fit for families bringing older relatives for a comfortable lunch, or groups of friends who want to sit with the river breeze and watch the riverside life at a slow pace.

The dish almost every table orders is the garlic-fried pla rad — a large whole fish, filleted and fried until crisp outside with tender meat inside, scattered with fragrant fried garlic. Most reviews agree that the fish is fresh, no muddy smell, with a natural sweetness. Another frequently mentioned dish is the tom yam pla ma and tom yam pla stomach — bold, rounded hot-sour broth. For curry-spice lovers, the fried-crisp pla nuea on in chu chi sauce and jungle-curry pla khang are worth trying — fragrant with herbs and properly hot. And for fried snacks, the fish cake (thot man pla krai) is described as wonderfully springy.

Prices are fair for river fish — stir-fries start around 70 THB; whole pla rad runs 250–360 THB; averaging 250–500 THB per person when eating in a sharing group. Located on the Sakae Krang riverfront, north side of the Phattana Phak Nuea Bridge, heading toward Ko Thepho, Mueang Uthai Thani District. Open daily from around 09:00 through 22:00. A riverside lunch in the breeze or an evening watching the sunset both hit differently.

What keeps this restaurant consistently popular is the freshness of fish that comes in from river boats almost daily, combined with the raft setting that's genuinely hard to find. A few notes: weekends and lunch rushes can mean limited staff and a slight wait for some dishes. Parking is fairly limited — arriving before the peak or calling ahead to book a riverside table makes things much smoother.
mustOrder: Tom yam pla ma / tom yam pla stomach
Chu chi fried-crisp pla nuea on
blocks.bestFor: Riverside river-fish meal with the family
blocks.spice: Medium–hot (tom yam / jungle curry dishes are properly hot)
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: street food · Charles Haynes / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 2.0)

blocks.name: Baan Nok Rim Na
blocks.signature: Salt-grilled pla chon served with dipping sauces and fresh vegetables, and garlic-fried pla rad
blocks.descHtml:
For anyone driving through Uthai Thani who wants a comfortable restaurant with a cool breeze, paddy field views, and lotus ponds, Baan Nok Rim Na in Nong Kha Yang is the place Uthai locals like to bring the whole family. Open for over ten years, the restaurant is fairly large, divided into an air-conditioned zone and an outdoor zone by the field with a wide car park. Suitable for a long relaxed lunch and an evening dinner with live music playing softly later in the night. The setting is genuinely rural — not staged — and widely rated as one of the better-standard restaurants in the province.

The dish to order is the salt-grilled pla chon — the restaurant's signature. Fresh fish, naturally sweet, served alongside a selection of dipping sauces and fresh vegetables as accompaniments. Multiple customers agree that the nam phrik (chilli dip) with fresh vegetables is particularly good. Another dish frequently ordered alongside is the garlic-fried pla rad — firm flesh, crisp outside, tender inside, mild enough for children. Beyond fish, there's also jungle curry with pla khang catfish, basket prawn salad with taro, nam phrik kapi with rice, salt-grilled chicken wings, and a house Baan Nok salad, so you can mix and vary across multiple visits.

Prices are approachable, around 101–250 THB per person — fish dishes priced by size. Genuine reviews note fresh ingredients, very fresh fish, fast food delivery, and good value for the quantity. Review scores sit around 3.9 stars, reflecting consistent overall satisfaction. Atmosphere and live music are regularly noted as highlights — good for long evenings without the music interfering with conversation.

Located at 15 Moo 2, Tha Pho Subdistrict, Nong Kha Yang District. Open daily 10:30–22:00. Booking by phone: 087-200-4998. Weekends can be busy — for large groups or if you want the field-side outdoor zone, calling ahead to book is the more comfortable option. For the live music, evening is the right time.
mustOrder: Salt-grilled pla chon (served with dipping sauces and fresh vegetables)
Jungle curry with pla khang catfish
blocks.bestFor: Family group dining, long relaxed sit by the field

blocks.name: Ya Jaew Coconut Ice Cream
blocks.area: Witthayu five-way junction, Mueang Uthai Thani District
blocks.cuisine: Thai desserts / old-school coconut ice cream
blocks.signature: Coconut ice cream with smooth, fragrant-rich texture, just a few baht a cup
blocks.descHtml:
Pa Jaew Ice Cream, or what most people call Ya Jaew Coconut Ice Cream, is the old-school coconut ice cream institution of Uthai Thani — in a small shophouse near the Witthayu five-way roundabout, close to the Sakae Krang River. Open for over 40 years since 1978, this is a must-stop for Uthai locals and dessert-trail visitors who want traditional coconut ice cream: firm texture, no artificial cream, where this is genuinely the real thing.

The dish to order is the coconut ice cream with full toppings — scooped into a cup with a choice of accompaniments: sticky rice, taro, pumpkin, lotus seeds, longan, drizzled with fragrant coconut cream. Or order it pressed into bread instead. Reviews from those who've been agree: the ice cream is smooth and soft, genuinely fragrant with real coconut, sweetness well-balanced and not sharp — a proper cool-down. Ya Jaew uses real coconuts from Thap Sakae, getting up at 2 a.m. every day to press the coconut cream herself, which is why the flavour is fresh and rounded in a way that's genuinely hard to replicate today.

Prices are as low as it gets — coconut ice cream with full toppings is 20 THB a cup; the bread version around 15 THB. A few baht and you have a cool dessert that satisfies. The setting is a small shophouse with a handful of tables inside and outside — casual, friendly, with the owner welcoming guests. Roadside parking available. An ideal cool-down stop during a walk through old-town Uthai.

The reason this place has lasted and stayed popular is consistent flavour and a genuinely old-style recipe that earned it the name "royal ice cream" (aisarim sawai) at some point. One thing to know: the shop opens mid-morning to around 17:00, and on some days may not be open every day or may sell out early. A midday to early afternoon visit is the safest window. Popular items can go fast on busy days.
mustOrder: Coconut ice cream with full toppings
Coconut ice cream pressed in bread
Coconut cream with sticky rice and lotus seeds
blocks.bestFor: Midday cool-down dessert stop on an old-town walk
blocks.hours: 10:00–17:00 (may not be open every day — check before visiting)

blocks.title: What to know before you eat in Uthai Thani

items.title: Walk most places easily
items.text: Most restaurants are in the old town and Trok Rong Ya area — all within walking distance of each other. Grab is limited in Uthai Thani city; renting a car or motorbike is recommended if you plan to visit river fish restaurants that are outside the main centre.

items.title: Carry cash
items.text: Most street spots and long-established restaurants only accept cash or PromptPay QR. Some don't have card machines at all. Having small bills prepared is the most convenient approach.

items.title: Go early to avoid selling out
items.text: Breakfast spots like Kotung and Jae Nok sell well and often run out before noon. For these, go in the morning to be safe. River fish restaurants fill up in the evenings on weekends — allow time to wait for a table.

items.title: Specify your spice level
items.text: The seafood dipping sauce and tom yam at the fish restaurants are quite bold. If you're not used to heat, ask the kitchen to reduce the chilli. Desserts and coffee are not spicy at all.

items.title: Menus are mostly Thai
items.text: Most local restaurants have Thai-only menus. Staff may have limited English. Pointing at photos or using a translation app works well. The sellers are friendly and will always point out the best dishes.

items.title: Tipping is not obligatory
items.text: Street spots and local restaurants don't expect a tip. At riverside restaurants with table service, leaving a small amount or rounding up the change is a nice gesture if you'd like to — not a fixed custom.

blocks.title: Planning a full day of eating in Uthai Thani
blocks.html:
Uthai Thani is small and most restaurants cluster in the old town and Trok Rong Ya — all within walking distance. Start breakfast at Kotung Khao Man Kai on Tha Chang Road (opens 06:00, closes mid-afternoon), then stop for Pa Thong's old-school coffee at 10 THB a cup nearby. Mid-morning, head to Jae Nok Chicken Noodles Trok Rong Ya — but go promptly because it often sells out before noon. Pick up sangkaya-filled bread from Phaiphan along the way as a snack to carry.

Later afternoon through evening, shift to the dessert and dinner side. Jae Da Fish Blanched opens from 15:30 near the Witthayu five-way junction; Ruean Phae Pramong and Baan Nok Rim Na are both great riverside dinner options with fresh Sakae Krang river fish. Close with Ya Jaew Coconut Ice Cream at a few baht a cup near the Witthayu five-way. If you have time mid-morning, TONE CAFE in Trok Rong Ya is worth a stop for the som za coffee signature drink.

blocks.text: Eating through Uthai Thani across morning and evening meals — staying the night makes everything more comfortable. Book a well-located stay in the old town first and walk to eat without rushing back.

faq.q: Which restaurant in Uthai Thani is most famous?
faq.a: The most talked-about are Kotung Khao Man Kai on Tha Chang Road — a Hainanese-style institution open since 1967, nearly sixty years — and Jae Nok Chicken Noodles Trok Rong Ya, an ancient recipe that sells out before noon. For desserts, Phaiphan Sangkaya Bread and Ya Jaew Coconut Ice Cream are the most well-known.

faq.q: What are the signature foods of Uthai Thani?
faq.a: The standouts are Hainanese khao man kai, ancient braised chicken noodles, sangkaya-filled bread, and Sakae Krang river fish like garlic-fried pla rad. There's also som za coffee — made from a local Uthai citrus — at TONE CAFE in Trok Rong Ya.

faq.q: How much does it cost to eat in Uthai Thani?
faq.a: Street food is very cheap — noodles and egg noodles run around 40–50 THB a bowl; khao man kai around 60–80 THB per person; old-school coffee 10–20 THB a cup. River fish riverside meals run higher, around 250–500 THB per person depending on what you order.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead?
faq.a: Most street spots and old-town restaurants are walk-in only — no booking needed. But riverside restaurants like Ruean Phae Pramong or Baan Nok Rim Na — if you're in a large group or coming on a long holiday weekend — a call ahead to reserve a table is more comfortable. Jae Nok should be visited early because items often sell out before noon.

faq.q: Which restaurants in Uthai Thani are open evenings or late?
faq.a: Morning spots like Kotung and Jae Nok close in the afternoon. Evening-focused spots include Jae Da Fish Blanched (around 15:30 through 21:00) and riverside restaurants like Ruean Phae Pramong and Baan Nok Rim Na, both ideal for dinner. Cafés and dessert spots mostly close in the evening — check opening times on each card before heading out.
